info.name: Fuel Route API
info.description: POST /api/v1/route/ — given a US start/finish location, returns the driving route plus a cost-optimal set of fuel stops for a 500-mile-range, 10-MPG vehicle. Requires the server running locally (`uv run python manage.py runserver`) with a valid ORS_API_KEY in .env for the requests that hit the real routing provider.

item.name: 1. Valid request — free-text locations (long route, multiple stops)

request.description: Free-text start/finish — the API geocodes both via ORS (in parallel, and cached for repeat requests), then calls ORS directions once. Expect HTTP 200 with a ~1080-mile route and several fuel stops (verified live: 5 stops, $168.64 total, gallons matching (distance-500)/10).

item.name: 2. Valid request — short route (no stop needed)

request.description: A route under 500 miles. Expect HTTP 200 with an empty fuel_stops array, total_gallons: 0, total_fuel_cost: 0 — the vehicle covers it on the starting full tank.

item.name: 3. Valid request — coordinates only (skips geocoding, 1 external call)

request.description: Same Chicago->Houston trip, but by coordinates. This skips both geocoding calls, so the whole request makes exactly 1 external API call (the ORS directions call) — the ideal case per the assignment's call-budget requirement.

item.name: 4. Invalid request — missing all required fields

request.description: Neither start/finish text nor all four coordinate fields supplied. Expect HTTP 400 with a validation error body.

item.name: 5. Invalid request — location that can't be resolved

request.description: A nonsense location string that ORS's geocoder can't resolve. Expect HTTP 400 with {"error": "Could not resolve location: Xzqwertyplace, ZZ"}.
